{{Short description|Mathematical logical symbol of 3 dots}}
{{Infobox symbol
|mark=∴
|unicode= {{unichar|2234|therefore|html=}}

In [[Argument|logical argument]] and [[mathematical proof]], the '''therefore sign''', '''{{char|∴}}''', is generally used before a [[logical consequence]], such as the conclusion of a [[syllogism]]. The symbol consists of three dots placed in an upright [[triangle]] and is read ''therefore''. While it is not generally used in formal writing, it is used in [[mathematics]] and [[shorthand]].

==History==
According to [[Florian Cajori]] in ''[[A History of Mathematical Notations]],'' the Swiss mathematician [[Johann Rahn]] used both an upright and an inverted triangle of dots to mean ''therefore''. In the German edition of ''Teutsche Algebra'' (1659), he used the upright triangle with its modern meaning, but in the 1668 English edition Rahn used the inverted triangle  more often to mean 'therefore'.{{r|Cajori1929|page=vol. 1, p. 211}} Other authors in the 18th century also used three dots in a triangle shape to signify 'therefore', but as with Rahn, there was little consistency as to how the triangle was oriented. Use of an upright triangle exclusively to mean ''therefore'' (and an inverted 
triangle exclusively to mean ''because'') appears to have originated in the 19th century. In the 20th century, the three-dot notation for 'therefore' became very rare in continental Europe, but it remains popular in [[Anglophone]] countries.<ref name=Cajori1929>{{cite book |last=Cajori |first=Florian |year=2011 |orig-year=1929 |title=A History of Mathematical Notations: Two Volumes in One |publisher=Cosimo, Inc. |isbn=978-1-61640-571-7 |pages=282–283 |url={{google books |plainurl=yes |id=gxrO8ZnMK_YC |page=282}} }}</ref>

==Examples of use==
Used in a [[syllogism]]:

:All gods are immortal.
:[[Zeus]] is a god.
:∴&nbsp;Zeus is immortal.

and in mathematics:

:{{math|1=''x'' + 1 = 10}}
:{{math|1=∴ ''x'' = 9}}

==Other uses==
===Meteorology===
In meteorology, a sign of three dots similar to the therefore sign is used to indicate "moderate rain" on a [[station model]]; the similar [[typography|typographic]] symbol [[Asterism (typography)|asterism]] (⁂, three [[asterisk]]s) indicates moderate snow.<ref>{{cite book |last=Ahrens |first=C. Donald |date=2011 |title=Essentials of Meteorology: An Invitation to the Atmosphere |edition=6th |publisher=Brooks/Cole |location=Belmont, CA |isbn=9780840049339 |oclc=651905769 |page=[https://archive.org/details/essentialsmeteor00ahre_508/page/n482 461] |url=https://archive.org/details/essentialsmeteor00ahre_508 |url-access=limited}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Station Model Information for Weather Observations |website=National Weather Service Weather Prediction Center |url=https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/html/stationplot.shtml |access-date=2019-07-16}}</ref>{{Clarify|date=May 2026 |reason=Are these actually the same symbols as the standard typographical symbols, or just similar? Does any source clarify this? The listed two, it seems, do not. Note that the depicted moderate rain dots seem much heavier than the therefore symbol is typically depicted.}}

===Freemasonry===
{{more|List of Masonic abbreviations#Typography}} 
[[File:DiplomeMaçonnique1945.png|thumb|A diploma from the Masonic ''[[Grande Loge de France]]'' showing the symbol as a substitute for the dot of abbreviation|alt=A diploma from the Masonic Grande Loge de France]]

In [[Freemasonry]] and certain related traditions, the symbol is used to indicate [[List of Masonic Abbreviations|a Masonic abbreviation]] (rather than the [[full stop|period]] mark used conventionally with some abbreviations). For example, "R∴W∴ John Smith" is an abbreviation for "Right Worshipful John Smith" (the term [[Right Worshipful]] is an honorific and indicates that Smith is a [[Grand Lodge]] officer).<ref name="Mackey">{{cite book |last=Mackey |first=Albert Gallatin |year=1925 |title=An Encyclopedia of freemasonry and its kindred sciences, comprising the whole range of arts, sciences and literature as connected with the institution |edition=reprint |publisher=Masonic History Co. |page=2}}</ref>

=== Anarchism ===
Originating from 19th ce French Anarchism, the three dot symbol is used as an anti-military and anti-authority signal, representing the French phrase ''[[:fr:Mort_aux_vaches_!|"Mort aux vaches!"]]'', which is equivalent to ''"Death to pigs"'' in English, although the original translates directly as ''"Death to Cows"''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-08 |title=Mort aux vaches! |url=https://www.sillonbelge.be/11087/article/2023-06-08/mort-aux-vaches |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Le Sillon Belge |language=fr}}</ref>

==Unicode==
The symbol has a Unicode [[code point]] at {{unichar|2234|therefore|html=}}. See [[Unicode input]] for keyboard-entering methods.

== LaTeX == 
One can write the symbol in [[LaTeX]]&nbsp;by using the <code>amssymb</code> package with the <code>\therefore</code> command.

==Similar signs==
{{Infobox symbol
|name = Similar signs
|mark=∵ ஃ ⁂ ⛬ ߷
|unicode= {{unichar|2235|because|html=}}<br />{{unichar|0B83|Sanskrit sign Visarga|nlink=Visarga}}<br />{{unichar|2042|Asterism|nlink=Asterism (typography)}}<br />{{unichar|26EC|Historic site|nlink=Japanese map symbol}}<br />{{unichar|07F7|NKo symbol Gbakurunen}}
}}

The inverted form, '''{{char|∵}}''', known as the '''because sign''', is sometimes used as a [[shorthand]] form of "because".

The character {{char|ஃ}} (visarga) in the [[Tamil script]] represents the [[āytam]], a special sound of the [[Tamil language]].

An [[asterism (typography)|asterism]], {{char|⁂}}, is a typographic symbol consisting of three [[asterisks]] ({{char|*}}) placed in a [[triangle]]. Its purpose is to "indicate minor breaks in text", to call attention to a passage, or to separate sub-chapters in a book.

A similar sign serves as a [[Japanese map symbol]] on the maps of the [[Geographical Survey Institute of Japan]], indicating a tea plantation. On some maps, a version of the sign with thicker dots, {{char|⛬}}, is used to signal the presence of a [[national monument]], [[historic site]] or [[ruins]]; it has its own Unicode code point.<ref>{{unichar|26EC|Historic site|html=|nlink=Japanese map symbol}}</ref>

In [[Norwegian language|Norwegian]] and [[Danish language|Danish]], a superficially similar symbol was formerly used as an explanatory symbol (''forklaringstegnet''). It can be typeset using the [[open o]] followed by a colon, thus: '''{{char|ɔ:}}'''. It is used for the meaning "namely", {{lang|la|id est}} ([[i.e.]]), {{lang|la|videlicet}} ([[viz.]]) or similar.<ref>{{cite web |title=Forklaringstegnet: en savnet del av det typografiske repertoar? |language=Norwegian |trans-title=Explanation: A missing part of the typographical repertoire? |website=www.typografi.org |url=https://www.typografi.org/forklaringstegn/forklaringstegn.html |access-date=2018-08-15}}</ref>

The punctuation mark {{char|߷}} (''gbakurunen'') of the [[N'Ko script]]—a modern [[writing system]] for the [[Manding languages]] of West Africa—is a paragraph mark which marks the end of a major section of text.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=NKo |url=https://www.unicode.org/charts/nameslist/n_07C0.html |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=www.unicode.org}}</ref> Its function is similar to that of the asterism.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-06-01 |title=N'Ko Alphabet: a West African Script {{!}} Cultures of West Africa |url=https://www.culturesofwestafrica.com/nko-alphabet-west-african-script/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230106041611/https://www.culturesofwestafrica.com/nko-alphabet-west-african-script/ |archive-date=2023-01-06 |access-date=2026-08-24 |work=Cultures of West Africa |language=en-US}}</ref> It symbolizes three stones holding a cooking pot over a fire.<ref name=":0" /> It is also used by internet users to pictorially represent a [[fidget spinner]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=߷ NKo Symbol Gbakurunen Emoji {{!}} Meaning, Copy And Paste |url=https://emojipedia.org/fidget-spinner |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=Emojipedia |language=en}}</ref>
